Resolves #21601

🌿 After this, an unanswered header measurement can no longer keep a newer layout off the screen.

A cold-boot Reset committed the Feed and never rendered it. The projection before it waited on a tab strip's natural-width read with no bound (`Reconciler.mjs`, both overflow recaptures), and every later commit queued behind that wait. Sophie's hold-and-release control (#21601, `issuecomment-7069886552`) reproduced the hosted signature exactly by holding that one read.

Now each commit creates its refresh's `AbortController` at the enqueue boundary (`Workspace#projectDockZoneDocument`) and aborts the one before it, whether that refresh is in flight or still queued. A refresh queued outside a commit (a repair, a parked replay, the tour's direct projection) joins the supersession current when it is queued (`Workspace#getProjectionAbort`), so the commit behind it releases that refresh too. The reconciler hands the signal to the overflow recaptures it starts. The overflow pass (`Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow#project`) races each await against the abort, hands its strip back as the last split left it, releases its latch, and leaves any queued re-run to the projection that superseded it. An answer that comes later writes no cache and no split. A superseded refresh still adopts its landed document, but it skips `releaseDeclaredPanes` and the presentation hooks, so an obsolete catalog cannot retire a pane the newer document restarts. The fence is Sophie's design from the ticket thread. The branch also stamps each step before the reconcile (`hostMounted`, `captured`, `released`), so a future miss names its phase.

Evidence: L3 (the real Workstation in local Chromium with the overflow read held through Reset, plus the unit tiers) → L3 required (AC-1; AC-2's local half). AC-2's three consecutive hosted `components` runs are this head's CI plus two reruns, listed under Test Evidence before review.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — 16 code lines (1073 → 1089): the three stamps before the reconcile, and the supersession fence (one AbortController per commit, created at the enqueue boundary where it also aborts the one before it; `getProjectionAbort`, which a refresh queued outside a commit joins; the signal handed to the reconciler; and the skip that keeps a superseded catalog from releasing panes). No consumer line to delete: no caller tracked a refresh's supersession before.

## Deltas from ticket

- No CPU throttling was needed: holding one overflow read reproduces the stall. The fix sits at that await, not in the transfer out of a headless workspace that The Fix guessed.
- The stamps ride here instead of in a leaf of their own, under the release's no-new-ticket direction.
- A superseded refresh no longer runs `releaseDeclaredPanes`, the collaborator syncs, the FLIP play or `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`. The refresh that supersedes it runs them against the current catalog.
- The Workstation's retained tab bars stay owned across a superseded refresh: `VesselWorkspace#animationSuppressedBars` keeps the bars a skipped `afterRefreshDockWorkspace` never restored, and the next refresh restores them after its own animation window. A bar that carried `neo-no-animation` before either refresh is never owned (Sophie's RA-1).
